Wiring the perfboard

From the breadboard to the board that goes in the case: about two and a half hours of soldering. Each step has a picture of the board as it should look when the step is done, and a hole map underneath that names every hole used, by its column (A–X) and row (1–18), as printed on the board. Both are drawn from the same layout, to scale. At the end you can turn the finished board round in 3D.

1

Before you start

⏱ 5 min

Do this once the breadboard test works end to end: every module has done what its test step said. The perfboard does the breadboard's job in a form that fits in the case: the ESP32 plugs into two sockets, and every module gets its own wires, soldered to the board.

You need

  • Double-sided prototype board, 70 × 50 mm, 24 × 18 plated holes on a 2.54 mm grid, used whole: no cutting. It sits on the four posts in the base with its front and back edges overhanging them.
  • Two 22-way 2.54 mm female header strips (cut longer strips with a knife, sacrificing one socket)
  • One 100 µF electrolytic capacitor, 10 V or more
  • Bare tinned wire (or resistor leg offcuts) for the bridges; thin insulated solid-core wire (wire-wrap or 26 AWG) for three links
  • Stranded 26 AWG hookup wire in several colours for the module wires, 22 AWG for the two power wires; female Dupont ends or crimp housings if your modules have pins
  • Two 220 Ω resistors and one 10 kΩ resistor (the same ones from the breadboard), heat-shrink
  • Soldering iron, solder, side cutters, multimeter

Every hole has a name, printed on the board: its column letter A–X counted from the left, then its row number 1–18 counted from the front. Hold the board with row 1 toward you, so the numbers count up away from you and the letters read left to right, whenever you read the pictures.

2

Solder bridges on the underside

⏱ 25 min

Turn the board over left to right, so row 1 is still toward you; column A is now on your right. That is how the underside pictures are drawn. Make each grey line by laying bare wire across the pads and soldering it to every pad it crosses (or by flooding solder from pad to pad on short ones).

  • Rows 16, 17 and 18, all 24 holes A–X: the power rails, along the back. Row 16 is 5 V, row 17 is 3.3 V, row 18 (the back edge) is ground. Use one straight piece of bare wire for each.
  • Rows 1–2–3 in columns E, F, G, H, I, J, K, M, P, Q, R, S, T, U: each joins an ESP32 pin (row 3, under its socket) to the hole two rows in front of it, where that pin's wire will go.
  • Rows 13–14–15 in columns E, F, G, H: the same for the back row of pins.
  • Columns not listed get no bridge: those ESP32 pins aren't used.
✅ Check: With the meter on continuity (beep): A18 to X18 beeps, and the same along rows 17 and 16. A16 to A17 and A17 to A18 must not beep, and nor may row 15 to row 16 in columns E–H. Then E1 to F1 (no beep), and so on for each pair of neighbouring signal columns. A beep between neighbours means a solder bridge where it shouldn't be: clean it with desoldering braid.
3

Three insulated links on the underside

⏱ 10 min

These connect the ESP32's power pins to the rails. Use insulated wire: each one crosses other bridges. Strip only the ends.

  • C3 → C17: 3.3 V: the ESP32's 3V3 pin to the 3.3 V rail.
  • B13 → B18: ground: the ESP32's G pin to the ground rail.
  • V3 → V16: 5 V: the ESP32's 5V pin to the 5 V rail.

Each runs straight along its column, mostly under where the ESP32 will sit. Lay it flat and keep it clear of the pads it crosses.

✅ Check: Beep test: C3 to X17 (3.3 V), B13 to X18 (ground), V3 to A16 (5 V). Then rows 16, 17 and 18 must still be silent to each other.
4

Sockets for the ESP32, and the capacitor

⏱ 15 min

Back to the top side. Push the two 22-way female headers into rows 3 and 13, columns B to W. Tip: plug them onto the ESP32 first and use the ESP32 as a jig, so they are exactly the right distance apart; solder one pin at each end, take the ESP32 out, then solder the rest.

⚠️ Don't plug the ESP32 in yet.

100 µF capacitor: long leg (+) in A16 (5 V rail), short leg and the stripe (−) in A18 (ground rail). It steadies the 5 V for the amplifier. Stand it up, under 11 mm tall.

✅ Check: Beep test, top side: each socket pin you bridged beeps to its pad two rows out (for example the socket in E3 to pad E1). The socket in C3 beeps to row 17, B13 to row 18, V3 to row 16.
5

Wires: Front display

⏱ 10 min

Wires for the TM1637 behind the front window. Cut each long enough to reach with the board in place in the case and the lid lifted off (about 15 cm for most; 25 cm for the lid and the projector, which has to reach the barrel's end). Strip 3 mm, push it into the pad from the top and solder it underneath. Label the far ends with tape as you go.

WirePadESP32 / supply
CLKE1GPIO 4
DIOF1GPIO 5
VCCD173.3 V
GNDI18ground

Wires: Lid: buttons, lights and light sensor

⏱ 10 min

Wires for the lid (see the lid harness below). Cut each long enough to reach with the board in place in the case and the lid lifted off (about 15 cm for most; 25 cm for the lid and the projector, which has to reach the barrel's end). Strip 3 mm, push it into the pad from the top and solder it underneath. Label the far ends with tape as you go.

WirePadESP32 / supply
SnoozeG1GPIO 6
Alarm 1 buttonM1GPIO 8
Alarm 2 buttonP1GPIO 9
Light sensorH1GPIO 7
Alarm 1 lightH15GPIO 41
Alarm 2 lightG15GPIO 42
3.3 VP173.3 V
GNDQ18ground

The three lid buttons, both alarm lights and the light sensor share one ground wire and the light sensor takes the only 3.3 V. Solder the 220 Ω resistors in the light wires right at each button's LED + tab and the 10 kΩ from the light sensor's signal leg to ground at the sensor, each covered with heat-shrink. That keeps the board simple.

Wires: Battery boards (optional)

⏱ 10 min

Wires for the charger and fuel gauge beside the battery. Cut each long enough to reach with the board in place in the case and the lid lifted off (about 15 cm for most; 25 cm for the lid and the projector, which has to reach the barrel's end). Strip 3 mm, push it into the pad from the top and solder it underneath. Label the far ends with tape as you go.

WirePadESP32 / supply
Charger CEQ1GPIO 10
Charger PGOODT1GPIO 13
Charger GNDS18ground
Gauge SDAE14GPIO 1
Gauge SCLF14GPIO 2
Gauge VINT173.3 V
Gauge GNDU18ground

Skip this group if you are not fitting the battery. The gauge's SDA and SCL go into E14 and F14, right in front of the clock module's E15 and F15: same pins, two wires. The gauge's wires ride over the clock module's holes as they leave.

12

Wires: Power in

⏱ 10 min

Wires for the 5 V boost (or straight to the USB-C breakout without the battery). Cut each long enough to reach with the board in place in the case and the lid lifted off (about 15 cm for most; 25 cm for the lid and the projector, which has to reach the barrel's end). Strip 3 mm, push it into the pad from the top and solder it underneath. Label the far ends with tape as you go.

WirePadESP32 / supply
5 V inW165 V
GND inX18ground

Use 22 AWG for these two. With the battery: from the boost's VOUT and GND. Without it: straight from the USB-C breakout's VBUS and GND.

13

All the wires at once

⏱ –

For checking: every wire and its pad. Wires leaving the front edge (row 1) go to the displays, the amplifier, the lid, button B and the charger; wires leaving the back edge carry power and ground (rows 16–18) and go to the clock module, the alarm lights and the battery gauge (rows 14 and 15).

Turn it round

Drag to turn the finished board, scroll or pinch to zoom.

14

Move the ESP32 over and test, one module at a time

⏱ 30 min

With nothing plugged into the sockets, check once more that rows 16, 17 and 18 don't beep to each other. Then:

⚠️ Never plug the USB-C supply and the ESP32's own USB port into power at the same time.
  1. Unplug the USB cable and lift the ESP32 off the breadboard. Plug it into the perfboard's sockets with its antenna end over column B and its USB ports at column W. Every pin must be in a socket: count that 22 pins sit in each row.
  2. Connect only the power wires and the front display. Power it from the USB-C supply. The front display shows the time within 30 seconds.
  3. Add the modules one at a time, powering off between each: projector display, amplifier, clock module, lid, button B, battery boards. After each, run that module's test from the breadboard guide.
  4. Open the clock's web page: status should show the clock module found, and with the battery boards a Battery line.
✅ Check: Everything that worked on the breadboard works here. If one module doesn't, its wires are the only new thing: beep each one from the module's pin to its pad.
15

Into the case

⏱ 10 min

The board sits on the four posts at the front right of the base, ESP32 USB end toward the right wall, row 1 toward the front. Slide it forward until its back edge clears the barrel's bearing block in the back-right corner: about 10 mm of the board then hangs past the front posts. Press it down until the two hooks on each short side click over its ends. Route the lid and projector wires up the right side, leave the battery and clock-module wires along the floor, and keep everything clear of the barrel, which turns. See the assembly steps for the rest.
